product.name: Sprigly
product.what: A liquid houseplant feed with seaweed extract, dosed with a measuring cap.
product.benefit: Feeding your houseplants takes one capful in the watering can every two weeks, with no guessing.
proof: Contains seaweed extract plus nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium (NPK 3-1-2)
Dose is one capful (5 ml) per litre of water
Label directions: feed every two weeks in spring and summer, monthly in autumn and winter
250 ml bottle makes 50 litres of feed
Glass bottle; refill pouches sold separately
product.label: SPRIGLY

audience.who: Adults in flats with a few houseplants who care about them but aren't expert gardeners
audience.moment: Sunday-morning watering, when they spot a droopy, pale-leaved plant on the windowsill and don't know what it needs
audience.pain: They water and hope, unsure how much to feed or how often, and feel quietly guilty when a plant looks tired

claims: One capful per litre: no measuring spoons, no guessing
Feed every two weeks in the growing season
Made with seaweed extract and NPK nutrients
One 250 ml bottle makes 50 litres of feed
noClaims: Promises any certain growth or result
Superlatives or rankings against other feeds
Organic, natural or eco-friendly claims beyond the listed facts
Plants double in size, or any specific growth figure
Urgency lines or scarcity talk about stock
tone: Warm and lightly funny: a deadpan two-hander between a guessing plant owner and a fern with opinions. No guilt, no scolding.
reason: The user's prompt fixes the product (Sprigly, 250 ml, one capful per litre every two weeks in spring and summer, fictional) and the original's standoff. Recreated as a voxel skit, the fern gets a voice, so the rule is said by the character who benefits from it. The proof points are the original's label facts; nothing promises a rescue, which the v1 and v2 audience tests flagged.
